ctx.x: I think George had a better ear and had much more technique than Tudie. That's an easy one for me.

In the bass playing department, there seems to have been a whole bunch of bass players that were a cut above the average, the ones that stayed in New Orleans. People talk about the trumpet players that left New Orleans, and the clarinet players were so much better. But the bass players... Like, you've got Wellman Braud, George Foster, Tudie Garland and Bill Johnson. All of them seem to have been so far in advance... However good they were technically, they seem to be so far in advance of people like Slow Drag and…

Oh, well, Slow Drag wasn't in the class of Braud or Pops Foster. Both of these guys got such huge... I listened to the tone, is what I used to like about Pops Foster, and his bowing and things like that.
